'''''Sedum praealtum''''', also known as '''shrubby stonecrop''' or '''green cockscomb''', is a small, woody [[succulent]] shrub in the [[stonecrop]] family that is native to [[Mexico]].<ref>[https://worldofsucculents.com/sedum-praealtum-green-cockscomb/ Sedum praealtum (Green Cockscomb)] by World of Succulents</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Gardenology.org-IMG 0478 hunt07mar.jpg|thumb|left|A clumping subshrub]]
It features sub-woody brown or grayish stems and fleshy, hairless leaves. It grows to 3 feet tall (90cm) and spreads to 4 feet (1.2m). The lime-green leaves are spatulated and are 1.5 inches (3.8cm) long, arranged in [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]]s. Large clusters of bright, star-like yellow flowers appear from late winter to spring. The plant tends to be summer-dormant.<ref>[https://www.succulentsandsunshine.com/types-of-succulents/sedum-praealtum-shrubby-stonecrop/ Sedum praealtum - Shrubby Stonecrop] Succulents and Sunshine LLC</ref> 

It is closely related to ''[[Sedum dendroideum]]'' and would look similar to it, but 'dendroideum' can be differentiated by the existence of a line of subepidermal glands on its margins near the leaf tips.<ref>[https://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=2555 Sedum praealtum - Bush Sedum] San Marcos Growers</ref>

==Cultivation==
It can be used as a [[bonsai]] due to its treelike appearance and it bears a resemblance to the [[Jade plant]].<ref>[https://succies.com.au/succulent-varieties/sedum/sedum-praealtum-green-cockscomb/ Sedum Praealtum (Green Cockscomb)] succies.com.au</ref> It easily grows in [[rock gardens]] in well-drained, poor soils. Propagation can easily be done by [[cuttings (plants)|cuttings]] and the plant is not cold hardy.<ref>[https://plantingman.com/sedum-praealtum-green-cockscomb/ Sedum praealtum (Green Cockscomb) – Succulent plants] Planting Man</ref>

==Uses==
A [[spermicide]] developed from this plant, that helps women control [[birth rate]]s without any major side effects, was around 20% more effective than [[nonoxynol-9]]. Its leaf substance has been traditionally used for burns, [[hemorrhoid]]s and [[dysentery]], [[gum inflammation]], and as well as an [[eye drop]] for [[conjunctivitis]] and irritations.<ref>[https://thetilth.com/sedum-praealtum/ Sedum Praealtum “Shrubby Stonecrop”] The Tilth</ref>
